title: Expressive Register and Affective Stylistics: Kosztolányi's Poetics

sections.title: Philosophical & Societal Framework
sections.content: Dezső Kosztolányi was not merely a poet and novelist; he was Hungarian literature's most passionate philologist-artist. In his legendary essays collected in *Nyelv és lélek* (Language and Soul), he argued that words have a physical body: weight, temperature, scent, and melodic cadence (*dallamosság*).

sections.title: Linguistic Analysis
sections.content: In 1933, when asked to select the ten most beautiful Hungarian words, Kosztolányi chose: *láng, gyöngy, anya, ősz, szűz, kard, csók, vér, szív, sír*. Notice that none of these are abstract foreign borrowings; they are primordial, mostly monosyllabic roots charged with existential, physical, and mythic resonance.
